reason: The hypothesis cites no prior evidence, and the key premises—especially the efficacy of yttrium oxide as defect sinks in refractory high-entropy alloys under fusion-relevant neutron conditions and the retention of mechanical properties—are specific claims requiring experimental support that is not provided.
premises: Yttrium oxide nanoparticles can be uniformly dispersed in refractory high-entropy alloys.
Yttrium oxide nanoparticles act as effective defect sinks for radiation-induced point defects and clusters.
Defect sink action by nanoparticles reduces void swelling and defect accumulation.
Reduction in radiation damage does not significantly degrade yield strength and ductility.
These effects are operative under fusion-relevant neutron irradiation at 500–1000°C up to ~10 dpa.
